Definition: from G575 and G71; to take off (in various senses):--bring, carry away, lead (away), put to death, take away.
BiblicalUsage: To lead away, to carry off, to bring before a judge. The soldiers lead Jesus away to the high priest, and the mob leads Him to Pilate. The word is the taking of a man where he does not choose to go.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for leading away carries no doctrine of its own; its sorrow is the passion's, that Jesus was led from one judgment seat to another for us.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Before the Sanhedrin; Jesus Before Pilate
